sources.title: Pavel Etingof and Mykola Semenyakin, A brief introduction to quantum groups
sources.locator: §2.1.3–2.2.2, PDF pp. 3–5: bialgebra/Hopf axioms, antipode identities and uniqueness, and the U_q(sl_2) coproduct/antipode formulas.
sources.reading_verification: Fetched and inspected the complete 43-page PDF and the full extracted text for §§2.1.3–2.2.2. The notes state the Hopf axioms, the anti-multiplicativity and uniqueness properties, and derive S(e)=-eK^{-1}, S(f)=-Kf, S(K)=K^{-1} for the same coproduct convention. This is rank one and does not check the type-A Serre relations; the new local lemma checks every type-A presentation relation and both antipode identities directly.

contents.name: Hopf axioms and antipode convention
contents.support: Supports the explicit antipode equations and sign convention. The source derives the rank-one formulas; the local proof supplies the type-A relation-preservation argument rather than importing the source's rank-one calculation as a proof of that claim.

contents.name: Type-A antipode candidate formula
contents.support: The source gives the same coproduct convention and generator formulas in U_q(sl_2); the item states the type-A word-reversing candidate explicitly and leaves quotient well-definedness to its local justifier.

contents.name: Two-site quantum coproduct convention
contents.support: The source confirms the coproduct convention used in the two-site calculation; the example evaluates the N=2 matrices locally and does not import a general commutation result.

sources.title: Li Luo and Weiqiang Wang, Lectures on dualities ABC in representation theory
sources.locator: §§2.1–2.2, PDF pp. 11–12, and §6.1, PDF pp. 30–31: classical Schur duality, the type-A Hecke action on tensor space, and the quantum double-centralizer statement.
sources.reading_verification: Fetched and inspected the complete 57-page v2 PDF and the full extracted text for §§2.1–2.2 and §6.1. Section 2.2 states the classical double-centralizer theorem and explicitly skips its proof; §6.1 gives the type-A Hecke generator action, parameter convention, and q-Schur double-centralizer statement with a deformation sketch. The local centralizer proof does not use the skipped classical proof or the q-deformation sketch: it supplies independent polarization/density/rank-specialization arguments. The Hecke convention is reconciled by noting that the notes' inverse-normalized generator acts by q^{-1} on repeated labels, whereas the library's T acts by q.

contents.name: Classical Schur duality and its double-centralizer formulation
contents.support: Provides an independent treatment of the classical action and double-centralizer statement. The notes refer elsewhere for its proof, so the local polarization and Newton-identity proof supplies the complete argument.

contents.name: Type-A Hecke action and q-Schur duality
contents.support: Supports the type-A Hecke tensor-action convention and the scope of the generic mutual-centralizer statement. The notes' representation-theoretic deformation sketch is not used as a proof; the local item proves the two rank sandwiches and separates the image equality from abstract faithfulness.

contents.name: Tensor-space Hecke normalization
contents.support: An independent treatment of the Hecke tensor operator. The library's T is the inverse-normalized convention, with equal-label eigenvalue q; the example calculates its matrix and all braid cases directly.

contents.name: Tensor-space Hecke action and generic faithfulness boundary context
contents.support: The notes state the general tensor-space action and double-centralizer context. Their theorem does not give this rank-one kernel computation; the counterexample proves it directly from the standard basis and one-dimensional action.

contents.name: Rank-two quantum/Hecke commuting calculation context
contents.support: The notes give the q-Hecke action convention; the local example explicitly computes both compositions for each of the four basis pairs and separately checks the Cartan generators.
